Clearing or changing the setting can disable the engine and withhold transfers through lines 199, 231 and 258.

conceptual assets.information: The prescaler selection and divider determine the one-wire transfer timing and sampling rate. The serial engine depends on this configuration to generate ticks and meet the protocol timing.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The bus can modify the prescaler and divider at lines 144-145, and those settings directly control tick generation at lines 260-265, so unauthorized changes can corrupt one-wire timing. Selecting an inactive source or an unsuitable divider can prevent tick generation and stall transfers through lines 260-265.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write an invalid prescaler or divider so that transfers use incorrect timing or never advance.

conceptual assets.information: The two-bit command selects whether a queued operation is a bit, byte or reset transaction. The serial engine depends on it to choose the one-wire operation and its sequencing.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: A bus write supplies the command field to the transmit FIFO at line 201, and the serial engine uses the returned command to select the operation at lines 331-336, so an attacker can change the requested transaction. The command can be withheld or discarded when the transmit FIFO is cleared or the engine is disabled through lines 199, 202 and 317-318.

conceptual assets.information: The eight-bit payload supplied with a queued bit or byte command is shifted and driven onto the one-wire bus. The transfer depends on this payload to communicate data to the attached device.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The payload may be secret to the integrating system and is exposed on the one-wire output through the serial drive assignments at lines 300 and 302. A bus write supplies the payload at line 201 and the serial engine loads and shifts it at lines 328 and 352, so unauthorized writes can change the transmitted value. Clearing or disabling the transmit path can withhold the payload through lines 199, 202 and 317.

conceptual assets.information: The byte sampled from the one-wire input is shifted into a receive result and returned to software through the receive FIFO and bus response. The IP depends on it to report data received from the attached device.

considered, not kept.reason: The request address, direction and strobe are access-command fields, while response acknowledge and error are handshake or constant status copies at lines 136-149 and 137, so they are not independent protected information.

Transmit-full, receive-available and busy values only report or time buffered data and sequencing state at lines 156-159, 196 and 228, which the FIFO-buffer and engine-status rules exclude as separate pieces.
The clear setting only clears the transmit and receive buffers at lines 199 and 231, so the port-buffer rule excludes it as an independent conceptual asset.
The serial state, bit counter and tick counter only order and pace transfer steps at lines 312-389, so the sequencing-state and pacing rules exclude them as information of their own.
The clock source and generated tick signals only advance the timing counter and serial steps at lines 260-268 and 360-367, so the clock and pacing rules exclude them as independent assets.
